knowledge:
- key_parameters: timeType=Set to "linear" if the experiment start time is meaningful (e.g., release into darkness), or "circular" if the start is unobserved/time-of-day ;; main_per=The main hypothesized period of interest (e.g., 24 for circadian studies) used to set defaults ;; cor_method=Correlation method ("pearson" or "spearman") used for pairwise inter-sample correlation outlier detection ;; threshold=Standard deviation threshold (typically 2 to 3) below/above the mean to flag outliers in correlation or PCA ;; aov_method=ANOVA method to test biological vs technical variation ("Equal Variance", "Welch", or "None") ;; avg_method=Method to combine technical replicates ("Mean", "Median", "Random Selection", or "None") ;; method/osc_method=Rhythm detection algorithm to run ("CS" for Cosinor, "JTK" for JTK Cycle, "LS" for Lomb-Scargle, "ARS" for ARSER)
- alternatives: Cosinor (CS)=Best for non-equidistant data and least-squares curve fitting ;; JTK Cycle (JTK)=Non-parametric, highly robust to outliers, offering greater sensitivity and specificity ;; Lomb-Scargle (LS)=Preferred for unevenly spaced time-series data ;; ARSER (ARS)=Removes linear trends, superior for short, noisy, and non-stationary time-series, but cannot handle missing values, biological replicates, non-integer intervals, uneven intervals, or circular time
- when_to_use: Appropriate for large-scale temporal biological datasets (e.g., circadian transcriptomic, proteomic, or metabolomic experiments) where the goal is to identify rhythmic features, estimate their period, phase, and amplitude, and detect sample outliers.
- pitfalls: Technical replicates must be combined (e.g., using discoRepAnalysis) before rhythm detection, as using them directly violates the independence assumptions of the statistical tests ;; Selecting a period based on exploratory period detection results can introduce selection bias and overfit, leading to inflated false-positive rates in downstream feature-wise testing ;; ARSER and JTK Cycle have strict experimental design restrictions (e.g., ARSER cannot handle missing values, biological replicates, non-integer intervals, uneven intervals, or circular time; JTK cannot handle non-integer or uneven intervals) ;; Rows with constant values or missing values are automatically removed during import

workflows.name: step_by_step_rhythm_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform a complete step-by-step rhythmicity analysis including data import, outlier removal, replicate merging, period profiling, and feature-wise oscillation detection.
input: temporal_data.csv (A CSV matrix with unique feature IDs in the first column and sample data in subsequent columns, where column names encode metadata as Prefix_Time_UniqueID_ReplicateID)
workflows.stages: 1. Import tabular data and convert to SummarizedExperiment using discoDFtoSE ;; 2. Clean data and check for missing/constant values using discoCheckInput ;; 3. Detect outliers using inter-sample correlation (discoInterCorOutliers) and PCA (discoPCAoutliers) ;; 4. Filter outliers from the SummarizedExperiment ;; 5. Analyze and combine technical replicates using discoRepAnalysis ;; 6. Detect dominant dataset-wide periodicities using discoPeriodDetection ;; 7. Perform feature-wise oscillation detection using discoODAs
workflows.code:
library(DiscoRhythm)
indata <- discoGetSimu()
se <- discoDFtoSE(indata)
selectDataSE <- discoCheckInput(se)
CorRes <- discoInterCorOutliers(selectDataSE,
                                cor_method="pearson",
                                threshold=3,
                                thresh_type="sd")
PCAres <- discoPCAoutliers(selectDataSE,
                           threshold=3,
                           scale=TRUE,
                           pcToCut = c("PC1","PC2","PC3","PC4"))
FilteredSE <- selectDataSE[,!PCAres$outliers & !CorRes$outliers]
ANOVAres <- discoRepAnalysis(FilteredSE,
                             aov_method="Equal Variance",
                             aov_pcut=0.05,
                             aov_Fcut=1,
                             avg_method="Median")
FinalSE <- ANOVAres$se
PeriodRes <- discoPeriodDetection(FinalSE,
                                  timeType="linear",
                                  main_per=24)
discoODAres <- discoODAs(FinalSE,
                         period=24,
                         method="CS",
                         ncores=1,
                         circular_t=FALSE)

workflows.name: batch_rhythm_analysis
workflows.intent: Execute the entire rhythmicity analysis workflow and generate an HTML report using a single batch function.
input: temporal_data.csv (A CSV matrix with unique feature IDs in the first column and sample data in subsequent columns, where column names encode metadata as Prefix_Time_UniqueID_ReplicateID)
workflows.stages: 1. Run the complete pipeline and generate an HTML report using discoBatch
workflows.code: discoBatch(indata=indata, report="discoBatch_example.html", ncores=1, main_per=24, timeType="linear", cor_threshold=3, cor_method="pearson", cor_threshType="sd", pca_threshold=3, pca_scale=TRUE, pca_pcToCut=paste0("PC",seq_len(4)), aov_method="None", aov_pcut=0.05, aov_Fcut=0, avg_method="Median", osc_method="CS", osc_period=24)
